synopsis: Existing public-api contains a real bounded official-page fetcher. It is restricted to curated source IDs and a fixed code-selected source list. The private feature runtime currently exposes bundled resource lookup and private-context read, while Codex configuration disables hosted web search. No current agent-directed live search/open path was found in the inspected provider/feature bridge.

criteria.evidence: Runtime web_search disabled; FeatureRunner resource tools offer bundled lookup only.

references.finding: fetchOfficialSource resolves curated source IDs, public HTTPS constraints, same-origin manual redirects, whole-request deadline, byte/text caps and text-only extraction. This is reusable real page-fetch infrastructure, not search discovery.
runRegionalAgent fetches code-selected cited source IDs from regional pack. Model receives fetched content afterward and cannot choose new URLs.
PublicEvidenceTools resource and guidance reads are bundled records; explicit needsReview and unknown activation preserved.
Resource feature offers find_official_resources and authorized context read; no agent-directed search/open dynamic tools in inspected code.

recommendations: Do not attest research true or call bundled lookup live grounding. Keep existing honest source/activation semantics.

Integration specialist should expose a justified real search capability and page-inspection bridge. Reuse bounded fetch policy where suitable, while permitting verified discovered public URLs rather than only a fixed source directory.
Preserve public/private query separation: send locality and actual service need to search, not medication/helper dossier. Bind results to URL, publisher, fetch date and source evidence IDs.

Before release require a live query with more than one candidate, actual selected page fetch, identity matching, comparison tied to family constraints, explicit unknown stock/activation/accessibility, and native follow-through. Route output to a fresh reviewer with exact inputs and criteria.

Public URL checks must consider DNS/internal-address resolution and redirect targets when extending beyond fixed allowlists; existing source-ID fetch policy is not by itself proof arbitrary discovered URLs are safe.
limitations: Source inspection only; no live web search or page retrieval performed, no source accuracy or research quality acceptance.
No production edits made by reviewer. Recommendations require specialist implementation and independent acceptance.
